notes: 2026-27 is the first season of a new DFB-Pokal media rights cycle (2026-27 to 2029-30). Germany: Sky keeps the pay-TV package with all 63 matches (48 exclusive), and the deal also covers Austria and Switzerland. 15 matches per season are free-to-air: ARD (Das Erste) has 7 plus the final every other season; ZDF and RTL share the other 7 plus the final in alternate seasons (ZDF's previous rights with ARD ended in 2025-26). Per DFB.de, RTL+ also streams all matches live as single games and in the Konferenz. Round 1 free-to-air: ZDF 1 match, ARD 2, RTL 3. Round 2 (27-28 Oct 2026): RTL HSV-Frankfurt, ZDF BVB-Bremen, ARD Bayern-Magdeburg. Which broadcaster has the 2027 final was not stated. International: the DFB's 15 Jun 2026 release lists a 'first wave' of partners for the new cycle, so other territories may follow. IMG Studios produces an English world feed of all 63 matches. The DFB also distributes its own OTT service 'DFB Play' and FAST channel 'DFB Play TV' in a growing number of (unspecified) territories. Gaps: no 2026-27 DFB-Pokal holder was found for the USA, Canada, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Poland, Belgium, Latin America outside Brazil, Australia, India or China.

broadcasters.note: Sky shows all 63 matches live (48 exclusive), as single matches and Konferenz, and DFB.de says RTL+ also streams all matches live. Free-to-air for selected matches only: 15 per season in total. ARD/Das Erste has 7 plus the final every other season; ZDF and RTL share 7 plus the final in the other seasons. Round 1: ARD showed Halle-Schalke and Osnabrück-Bayern, ZDF Rostock-Stuttgart, and RTL HEBC-BVB, Saarbrücken-Hertha and Würzburg-Köln. Round 2: RTL HSV-Frankfurt (27 Oct), ZDF BVB-Bremen (27 Oct), ARD Bayern-Magdeburg (28 Oct).

Sky's 2026-27 to 2029-30 DFB deal covers Austria (Sportcal, May 2025). ServusTV (free-to-air, presumably selected matches) is listed only by the comparison portal sportabo.at (Oct 2026) and is not confirmed by the DFB or ServusTV.

Sky's 2026-27 to 2029-30 DFB deal applies across all distribution channels in Austria and Switzerland as well as Germany. moneyland.ch (Sept 2025) also listed DAZN for the DFB-Pokal in Switzerland, which is not confirmed for 2026-27. No free-to-air broadcaster found.
